name: RankRocket Connector
author: ddabush

sections.description:
RankRocket Connector is the secure WordPress bridge for the RankRocket service. It establishes an authenticated connection and exposes allowlisted REST API endpoints used by RankRocket.

WordPress administrators can also use the built-in RankRocket page manager without connecting an account or running an audit. The local manager can preview and apply supported page, post, product, custom-post-type, and taxonomy SEO changes. Post changes create a verified native WordPress revision first and can be restored from the same screen.

The connector can:

  • Report connection, WordPress, and plugin status
  • Provide supported site and page data for administrator-requested RankRocket workflows
  • Receive authenticated requests for approved WordPress operations
  • Coordinate full-site restore points with UpdraftPlus before approved updates
  • Locally manage H1 and H2 headings, SEO titles, meta descriptions, image alt text, robots directives, canonical URLs, and existing FAQ schema
  • Preview local changes and create, inspect, and restore native WordPress page revisions

SEO analysis and solution generation happen in the RankRocket service, not in this plugin. The connector does not independently crawl the site, generate recommendations or content, or run an AI model.

Before a supported update, RankRocket verifies the audit’s full-site backup in private RankRocket storage. WordPress backup archives are streamed without placing RankRocket cloud credentials on the site. RankRocket does not apply a change until an administrator approves it and the matching backup is verified.

External service

This plugin connects to RankRocket, a software-as-a-service SEO platform. A RankRocket account is required to use the connected automation features.

When an administrator connects a site or requests an SEO operation, RankRocket may receive the site URL, WordPress REST URL, WordPress and plugin versions, selected public page URLs, page content and headings, SEO metadata, image URLs and alternative text, structured data, connection status, and operation results. This data is sent only as part of an administrator-initiated connection, audit, preview, apply, restore, or related RankRocket workflow. WordPress passwords, cookies, payment information, and unrelated private content are not intentionally sent.

RankRocket sends authenticated, structured requests back to this plugin to read supported SEO data or apply approved changes. The plugin does not download or execute remote PHP, JavaScript, SQL, or other executable instructions from RankRocket.

Service website: https://www.rankrocket.info/

Privacy Policy: https://www.rankrocket.info/privacy-policy/

Terms of Use: https://www.rankrocket.info/terms-of-service/
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate RankRocket Connector.
  2. Open RankRocket in the WordPress admin menu to use the local page manager.
  3. To use connected audits and automation, generate an API key or complete the connection flow from your RankRocket account.
  4. Use the connected RankRocket service to review and approve supported WordPress operations.
sections.faq:
Is a RankRocket account required?

An account is required for connected RankRocket audits and automation. The local WordPress administration tools remain available to authorized administrators.

Does RankRocket make changes automatically?

No. Changes require an authorized administrator action or an authenticated request resulting from an approved RankRocket workflow.

Does the plugin generate SEO solutions?

No. Analysis and solution generation happen in the RankRocket service. This plugin provides the authenticated connection to WordPress and implements allowlisted WordPress operations.

How is the REST API protected?

Protected routes require a configured RankRocket API key sent in the X-RankRocket-Key header, an authorized WordPress session, or an authenticated WordPress Application Password, depending on the route. Site-wide changes require administrator capability; Editor-level Application Passwords can access only the read-only page-discovery route. Administrative actions also use WordPress capability and nonce checks.

Can I undo a RankRocket change?

Yes. RankRocket can restore a verified full-site backup created for an audit. A restore replaces later database and file changes, so RankRocket displays a clear warning and creates a recovery backup first.

Does the plugin execute code received from RankRocket?

No. It accepts only structured values for allowlisted WordPress operations implemented in the plugin.

What happens if another SEO plugin is active?

RankRocket uses its own metadata and integrates with supported SEO providers where appropriate. Review previews and final page output after each change, especially when multiple SEO tools manage the same field.
sections.changelog:
3.7.13

  • Keep RankRocket Connector automatically updated through the official WordPress.org release channel.

3.7.12

  • Keep full-site backup status checks responsive by deferring archive checksums to RankRocket’s verified transfer process.

3.7.11

  • Fix Elementor H1 and H2 operations so they update and verify live builder data.
  • Prevent unsupported Elementor heading operations from reporting false success.

3.7.10

  • Cleans up stale UpdraftPlus restore folders after verified artifacts are ready so rollback and automatic recovery can proceed safely.

3.7.9

  • Removes RankRocket-managed FAQ content reliably when its wrapper includes alignment classes.

3.7.8

  • Adds administrator-authenticated site-manager APIs for safe page inspection, previews, and allowlisted manual operations.
  • Adds stale-state protection, exact image targeting, and idempotent remote operation handling.
  • Reports the WordPress site title with backup health for website-specific restore points.

3.7.7

  • Restores the administrator-only local SEO operations screen independently of RankRocket audits.
  • Restores local previews plus native WordPress revision creation, inspection, and rollback.
  • Repairs H2 actions and validates taxonomy canonical URLs before saving.
  • Scopes local previews and rollback to managed fields and restores linked media alt changes without replacing unrelated product data.

3.7.6

  • Prevent duplicate meta-description tags when another supported SEO plugin is active.
  • Reject non-HTTP canonical URLs at both the REST and storage boundaries.

3.7.5

  • Restore the SEO-override classification helpers required by request-scoped mutation verification.
  • Prevent mutation-state capture failures from leaving persistent target locks.
  • Clear abandoned request-scoped mutation locks safely when the Connector is activated.

3.7.4

  • Keeps the active restore job and current authorization available while UpdraftPlus replaces the WordPress database.

3.7.3

  • Preserve host-managed WordPress language packs while restoring all other verified site content.

3.7.2

  • Resolves imported UpdraftPlus restore points by their immutable backup nonce when filename reconstruction rounds timestamps to the minute.
  • Rejects mixed or malformed restore artifact sets before WordPress files are changed.

3.7.1

  • Accepts the canonical www or non-www alias only when it resolves to the same protected WordPress installation.
  • Continues rejecting unrelated subdomains and external origins before protected fixes.

3.7.0

  • Replaces persistent page-level RankRocket versions with verified full-site UpdraftPlus restore points.
  • Adds a stable WordPress installation identifier and strict fix-target ownership validation.
  • Adds local-only backup, artifact transfer, restore staging, progress, and health endpoints.
  • Removes RankRocket-owned legacy history metadata and marked snapshot revisions.

3.6.62

  • Allows an approved specific image to be marked decorative with an explicit empty alt attribute.

3.6.61

  • Restores the previous stable FAQ generation, preview, and publishing workflow.
  • Removes the experimental intelligent FAQ placement and styling workflow.
  • Keeps the existing connector, update, and Simple Mode integrations unchanged.

3.6.53

  • Maintenance release to refresh the WordPress.org connector package.

3.6.52

  • Adds administrator-approved one-click updates for the official WordPress.org connector.
  • Adds an opt-in setting for WordPress core automatic connector updates.
  • Restricts managed updates to the fixed RankRocket Connector plugin and official WordPress.org packages.

3.6.51

  • Publishes the current RankRocket Connector through the standard WordPress.org update channel.
  • Keeps connector behavior unchanged from version 3.6.50.

3.6.50

  • Confirms Elementor image-alt data by reading the exact saved document data back after each update.
  • Lets Simple Mode invalidate only the edited page’s Elementor rendered HTML cache.
  • Preserves Elementor CSS, generated files, shared templates, and global Elementor caches.
  • Clarifies that this plugin is the secure WordPress connector and does not generate SEO solutions.

3.6.48

  • Preserves Elementor-generated CSS while purging updated RankRocket page and site caches.
  • Prevents cached Elementor templates from temporarily rendering without their responsive styles after SEO updates.
  • Regenerates or invalidates only the restored Elementor document when a rollback changes builder layout data or page settings.

3.6.47

  • Loads preview JavaScript and CSS through WordPress enqueue APIs.
  • Uses WordPress output APIs and late sanitization for FAQ and JSON-LD rendering.
  • Replaces request-wide output buffering with scoped content and image filters.
  • Keeps RankRocket settings in RankRocket-prefixed storage.

3.6.46

  • Prepares the RankRocket Connector package for WordPress.org distribution.
  • Requires administrator capability for site-wide REST operations.
  • Safely normalizes stored JSON-LD before rendering it in page output.

3.6.45

  • Improves rollback previews after a prior restore.
  • Distinguishes legacy live fallbacks from saved historical values.
  • Uses metadata from the active SEO provider when presenting previous values.

3.6.44

  • Shows the previous visible SEO value when restoring removes a RankRocket override.

3.6.42

  • Adds a bounded RankRocket version history with an Original and latest Last Change for each supported target.
  • Adds atomic rollback, conflict detection, failure compensation, and verification.
  • Supports posts, custom post types, taxonomies, virtual archives, page builders, structured data, and media alt text.

3.6.41

  • Adds RankRocket-managed JSON-LD insertion for supported schema opportunities.

3.6.40

  • Refreshes the production plugin package and version metadata.
